name: blue heraldic banners on iron rods and a blue-and-gold shield hung flat on an ashlar town wall face (gold crown over a gold eight-point star)
label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_wall_heraldry

surfaces.part: ashlar wall face (stone courses, background body)
upper wall band / parapet-like grey strip with notched top
iron rods (thin horizontal bars)
left blue banner (vertical cloth with crown and star)
blue-and-gold shield (flat)
right blue banner (vertical cloth with crown and star)
base ledge band

answer.evidence: The whole piece is a flat, face-on wall elevation. Banners, shield and rods are vertical faces hung flat on the ashlar wall, with no depth or receding side face. The wall carries only thin horizontal rows: a 1-row light coping line at row 1, a 1-row dark line at row 31, and a 2-row light band at rows 84-85. None of these is a deep top plane, and there is no ellipse, roof or visible contents. The face reads as a front elevation. That is expected for a flat wall-mounted object, but there is no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ashlar wall is shaded stone by stone, with highlight, light, mid, dark and mortar tones, plus speckle and grass tufts at the base. This matches the Beodeul hedge and well in texture. Measured facts support this: 12 visible tones per tile sits inside the reference range (hedge 9, cheese stall 17, well 20), and near-flat coverage is 0%. The banners and shield are the thinnest part, at about 3-4 blue and gold steps. They have dark blue-tinted edges with value separation rather than a black sticker line, and the stone edges lean brown-grey. The 46% neutral share of dark edge pixels is close to the bench (44%) and well (33%), so I call the outline mixed rather than near-black. The piece is a wall face rather than a standing prop, but its craft is comparable to the references. It does not look flatter or thinner next to them.

The 1-2 row light band at rows 84-85 is only a ledge strip. The main body has no top surface and a full-height front face, so it reads as front elevation, which is acceptable for a flat wall-mounted kind.
